record.paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
record.original_question: Characterize all classical multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} that admit a C_k-representation. This means that there exist not-necessarily-distinct functions phi and Phi in L-P+ and real parameters s,t such that gamma_k=C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s) for every k>=0, where B_k^phi(t)=sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j)(1-t)^j gamma_{k-j} t^{k-j} when phi(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/k!, and C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s)=sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s). Here L-P+ is the nonnegative-coefficient part of the Laguerre-Polya class, and a classical multiplier sequence is a real sequence whose diagonal operator preserves real-rootedness of real polynomials.

evidence.quote: Definition 31. Let gamma_k in R for k = 0, 1, 2, .... We say that the sequence {gamma_k}_0^infinity has a C_k-representation, if there exist functions phi, Phi in L - P+ (not necessarily distinct) and s, t in R such that gamma_k = C_k^{phi,Phi}(t, s) for all k in N_0, where C_k^{phi,Phi}(t, s) is as defined in equation (4.2).
C_k^{phi,Phi}(t, s) := sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s).
B_k^phi(t) = sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j)(1 - t)^j gamma_{k-j} t^{k-j}.
Problem 44. Characterize all multiplier sequences which have a C_k-representation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ denote the subclass of the Laguerre–Pólya class consisting of entire functions that are locally uniform limits of polynomials with only real, non-positive zeros; equivalently, entire functions of the form $\phi(x)=Cx^n e^{\alpha x}\prod_{k}(1+\alpha_k x)$ with $C\ge 0$, $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $\alpha\ge 0$, $\alpha_k\ge 0$, and $\sum \alpha_k<\infty$. Such functions have a power series $\phi(x)=\sum_{k\ge 0}\gamma_k x^k/k!$ with all $\gamma_k\ge 0$.

A real sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is called a classical multiplier sequence if, for every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k$ whose roots are all real, the polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^n \gamma_k a_k x^k$ also has only real roots.

For $\phi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ with $\phi(x)=\sum_{k\ge 0}\gamma_k x^k/k!$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}$, define
$$B_k^{\phi}(t)=\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j}(1-t)^j\,\gamma_{k-j}\,t^{k-j},\qquad k\ge 0.$$
For $\phi,\Phi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ and $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$, define
$$C_k^{\phi,\Phi}(t,s)=\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j}B_j^{\phi}(t)\,B_{k-j}^{\Phi}(s),\qquad k\ge 0.$$

Say that a real sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ admits a $C_k$-representation if there exist functions $\phi,\Phi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ (not necessarily distinct) and real numbers $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $\gamma_k=C_k^{\phi,\Phi}(t,s)$ for every $k\ge 0$.

Problem: Characterize all classical multiplier sequences that admit a $C_k$-representation.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open characterization problem in the survey context. No subsequent paper providing a full characterization of classical multiplier sequences admitting a $C_k$-representation could be located, so the problem appears to remain open.
